In our universe Maxwell’s equations (in vacuum) are  

1. ∇·E = ρ/ε₀           (Gauss’s law for E-field)  
2. ∇·B = 0               (Gauss’s law for B-field)  
3. ∇×E = −∂B/∂t       (Faraday’s law: circulation/curl of E-field)  
4. ∇×B = μ₀J + μ₀ε₀∂E/∂t   (Ampère–Maxwell law: circulation/curl of B-field)

If magnetic monopoles could exist (isolated north or south poles), we would have a magnetic charge density ρₘ and a magnetic current density Jₘ. To accommodate these new sources the symmetric form of Maxwell’s equations becomes

1. ∇·E = ρ/ε₀                                 (unchanged)  
2. ∇·B = μ₀ρₘ                                (now non-zero divergence)  
3. ∇×E = −∂B/∂t − μ₀Jₘ                   (curl/circulation of E gains a term)  
4. ∇×B = μ₀J + μ₀ε₀∂E/∂t                 (unchanged)

Thus the equations that are altered are:

• Gauss’s law for the magnetic field (divergence of B), and  
• Faraday’s law (curl/circulation of the electric field).

That corresponds to option (B): “The ones related to the circulation of the electric field and the divergence of the magnetic field.”

Answer: B
